summary: The same-artifact revision's two schema facts (cinatra#3030, epic #3023 W6; plan (C) item 0.30). ONE: the artifact_produced_outbox emitter CHECK gains 'artifact_revision_append' — a mid-run write that appends the next revision of an existing artifact is not the road that minted it, and the closed emitter set is the audit surface, so one emitter standing for both would make 'was this artifact created here or revised here' unanswerable on the row. TWO: a new artifact_revision_review_satisfaction table keyed on (org_id, artifact_id, representation_revision_id) with run_id and review_task_id — item 0.30's satisfaction rule, 'the caller's own declared gate is recorded as the review of those revisions, and the produced-output road, when it fires, resolves to that gate instead of opening a second'; the primary key IS the rule, one revision names exactly one satisfying gate, and run_id records whose gate satisfied it so a caller can only ever name a gate of its own run. The CHECK widen is a PURE WIDENING: every value the old predicate accepted the new one accepts, so no committed row can become invalid, no row is rewritten, and the ADD CONSTRAINT's re-validation scan passes by construction. Idempotent twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL in artifactReviewGateSchemaQueries (src/lib/artifacts/artifact-review-gate-schema.ts), shipped in the SAME pull request (core__0099 / core__0103 precedent). down() has two halves: the CHECK narrows back to the four-emitter vocabulary and FAILS loudly on an instance that has already appended a revision (deleting an outbox row to make a revert succeed would drop a review the product opened), and the satisfaction table is dropped ONLY when empty — a non-empty table records which gate reviewed which revision and the down raises rather than erase it. SEQ 0104 — core__0103 is the highest sequence on main at authoring time. DECLARED DESTRUCTIVE: the new table is purely additive, but REWRITING the emitter CHECK on a deployed table is the core-store schema migration gate's own add-constraint rule, and the operator-upgrade artifact for that rewrite is this migration.
